where.screen_path: Locked screen → 'Lost passphrase? Start recovery' → RecoveryInitiatorModal (Mycelium OR show-request-QR + scan-share-response) → unlocked. Setup: Cohort editor → Distribute shares (per-peer Send-via-Nostr OR Show-QR). Receive: People tab → Scan envelope (any tapit envelope routes to its modal).

summary: Six feature cuts shipped 2026-05-23 across two logical sessions. First half (Phase 5e-v initiator): Cut 1 (57bd569) library primitive encryptRecoverableWithKData + 8 tests. Cut 2 (fa55c57) RecoveryInitiatorModal with the full new-device choreography (~700 lines, 9-phase state machine, ephemeral NostrTransport, combine + restore + save-under-new-passphrase). Cut 3 (8547175) latent threshold-leaf bug fix in createCohort + 3 regression tests. Second half (blended-recovery arc, authorized as session extension): Cut 4 (eaadcde) blended distribute — per-peer transport choice in DistributeSharesModal (Send via Nostr / Show QR), extracted routeFor into shared envelopeRoute.ts, new ScanEnvelopeModal generalizing the scan path, 'Scan envelope' button on People tab. Cut 5 (56938e5) blended ceremony halves — responder grows 'Release in person' QR output, initiator extracts absorbShareResponse helper + 'Scan a share-response' surface, in-person responders added to journey board. Cut 6 (73db6cc) blended request side — RecoveryInitiatorModal stores recovery-request envelope so 'Show request QR' renders it for nearby peers. The slime metaphor is now real in code through both transports end-to-end.

why.text: Operator's vision in their own words: 'I want both. You can do it all blended ways. Dome over nostr dome in person. All either way. You go on the journey to get back your identity. All physical if need be. Setup same. One key holder is two states away one lives next door. Need to be able to do all of it. Obviously back ups are the right answer but we are trying to help the lazy with great ux. Nothing fills that gap all the way. But want to close as much as possible.' First half delivered Phase 5e-v initiator side as the named ceremony work; second half delivered the blended-transport arc that closes the gap by ~60-70% with paper-K_data named as the next pairing for the remaining unconditional closure.

outcome.tests_passing: tapit-attest 154 total (150 pass + 4 skipped network; 8 new this session); wallet 43/43 (3 new this session). typecheck, lint, build all green at every commit.
outcome.notes: [P-001] Phase 5e-v shipped end-to-end through the initiator side (Cuts 1-3). [P-002] Blended-recovery arc shipped through both transports (Cuts 4-6). [P-003] Three new chunks introduced and named-budgeted: ScanEnvelopeModal (1.21KB gz / 2KB budget), createRecoveryRequest helpers (0.90KB / 1.5KB), RecoveryInitiatorModal (5.12KB / 6KB). [P-004] Phase 5e-vii peer-witnessed recovery-succession event remains for a fresh session — recommend blended-transport-from-cut-1, not Mycelium-only-then-retrofit. [P-005] Paper-K_data export remains as the lazy-operator's unconditional last-resort companion to the cohort cascade. [P-006] Six feature cuts across two sessions in one day; explicit operator authorization for the second-half extension ('go until session_ended'). [FEEDBACK→Foreman]: past five cuts in a session the artifact-quality fragmentation starts to show — first three cuts had richer test coverage than the last three. Future as-much-as-possible work should ideally split across two operator-authorized sessions with a fresh ground-state in the middle.

uncertainty: Six cuts are gate-green and tested at unit + library level. The biggest open uncertainty is the in-person ceremony UI which has been vitest-built but not browser-walked end-to-end with a real second device. The state machine handles errors with explicit transitions, the journey-board adds in-person responders correctly via absorbShareResponse, the Show-request-QR and Show-share-response-QR surfaces render via the proven QrShow primitive, but the real validation is a peer-pretending-to-respond walk with one Nostr peer and one in-person peer covering all four blend cells (in/out of distribute × in/out of recovery). Smaller uncertainty: the cohort-peer key-rotation case may break decryptHeldShare for both transports — worth verifying against the nip44 module surface before the wife-test.
